text:
jess: quick heads-up — ran a hybrid kernel affinity experiment against the paged-attn path on staging (FlashV2 vs FlashLite + fused path). piling notes here, want 👀 before i open a formal ticket

sam: nice, high level results first?

jess: TL;DR: FlashV2 wins p50 in long-seq (2k tokens) but FlashLite + fused wins p99 under memory pressure due to lower kv-pager churn. throughput differences small (~3-7%).

lee: can you paste the perf numbers?

jess: sure — run details: 8x A100, batch=4, beam=1, ctx=2048/4096/2048 (seq mixes). workload = mixed chat + doc-summarize probes.

perf-bot: benchmark summary: 
```
config: hybrid-affinity-v1
model: ggml-flashvariant-13b
kernels: FlashV2, FlashLite, FusedAttn
seq-mix: {short: 60%, mid: 30%, long: 10%}
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec
```
results:
FlashV2: p50=34ms p95=210ms p99=560ms tokens/s=1800
FlashLite+Fused: p50=38ms p95=190ms p99=320ms tokens/s=1680
under mem-pressure (kv-pages active): FlashV2 p99 -> 980ms (lots of page thrash)
```

marta: flashv2 p99 jump is concerning. was the KV cache allocation policy default?

jess: yes default: slab allocator with eager slot reservation. we tried two allocation tweaks in the same run: (A) freelist-segmentation (B) lazy-prefault.

sam: quick explainer — freelist-segmentation?

jess: split free pool by blocktable age buckets so new slots come from young bucket first, reduces migrating hot KV between blocks. lazy-prefault delays physical page mapping until first use which reduces initial memory pressure spikes when many sessions start concurrently.

lee: and which combination reduced p99?

jess: best was FlashV2 + freelist-segmentation + lazy-prefault: p99 -> 360ms (vs 980ms). tokens/s stable at 1750.

marta: interesting. any regressions on p50?

jess: minor increase p50 ~+6% — acceptable trade for tail. also saw fewer page-eviction flurries in pagehouse telemetry.

sam: were there any kernel-selection flips causing misrouting? e.g., runtime choosing FlashV2 then falling back causing extra cost?

jess: yes we observed ~2% of requests experiencing kernel flip when seq estimate changed mid-request (early next-token hints). flips mostly happened when initial seq flagged fused path but increased token generation forced FlashV2 kernel. flip cost ~120ms on average.

lee: can we make kernel affinity sticky per-request or per-session to avoid flip?

jess: tested affinity-ttl=1s and affinity-ttl=30s. ttl=30s removed flips but increased p99 for short seqs because they stayed on slower kernel. optimal seems to be affinity-ttl=3s + flip-penalty-check (reject flip unless expected win > 15% latency).

perf-bot: telemetry snippets: 
- block-table fragmentation: mean 18% free spread, tail 52%
- avg kv-slot migration per-minute: default 120 -> freelist-seg 18
- pagehouse I/O spikes per-hour: default 9 -> freelist-seg 1

marta: those migration numbers are huge. have you profiled hot path in runtime? flame graphs?

jess: yes, attached stack dump pasted below (abridged):
```
- dispatch_request()
  - kernel_selector::evaluate()  (15%)
  - kv_cache::lookup_or_allocate() (28%)
  - blocktable::evict_if_needed() (22%)
  - attention_runner::execute_kernel() (25%)
  - telemetry::emit() (5%)
```
hotspot is lookup_or_allocate and evict_if_needed. freelist-seg moved cost out of eviction into lightweight list ops.

sam: small implementation question — freelist-seg increases metadata per-block? memory overhead?

jess: about +1.4% RAM for metadata on our 13B config, negligible compared to paging savings.

lee: how deterministic are these results vs different seq mixes?

jess: reran with long-heavy mix (30% long) — FlashV2 throughput advantage widened 9% but p99 without freelist was catastrophic (1.8s). freelist + lazy-prefault kept p99 ~400ms and throughput ~1730 tokens/s.

marta: what about garbage compaction for blocktable? any compaction pauses?

jess: compaction runs in background w/ soft-yield. we observed small pauses when compaction clashing with eviction under peak. we added a compaction hysteresis threshold (dont compact unless free<12%) which eliminated the 30-50ms micro-pauses.

perf-bot: config snippet used for allocator: 
```
{
  "kv_allocator": "freelist-seg",
  "seg_buckets": [0-5m,5-30m,30m+],
  "lazy_prefault": true,
  "compaction_hysteresis_pct": 12
}
```

sam: next steps? do we want this as default in staged Dedicated?

jess: propose feature flag rollout: stage -> canary on dedicated -> default. also add kernel affinity policy change (3s ttl + win-threshold).

marta: +1. let's add e2e evals for coldstart-heavy traffic (PLG bursts) and also regression tests for flip penalty.

lee: please open RFC+benchmark artifact. i'll help with e2e harness.

jess: will do — creating RFC & PR this afternoon. i'll tag you all. thanks! :rocket:
